title: David Naccache
name: David Naccache
summary: French cryptographer and ENS researcher whose work spans public-key cryptography, embedded-system security, code security and digital forensics.
whyThisMatters: Naccache's work joins cryptographic construction with the realities of constrained devices and physical attack surfaces. That bridge matters wherever cryptography is implemented in smart cards, mobile devices and embedded products.

sections.overview:
Research and practice

David Naccache heads the Information Security Group at ENS Paris. The group's profile describes research interests including code security, forensics and vulnerability detection, alongside a career in industry at Gemplus, Philips and Thomson.

Cryptography for embedded systems

Naccache has published on practical public-key constructions, signatures and the security of embedded systems. ENS's CASCADE research material identifies work on cryptography for embedded-system security, including privacy and integrity of code and confidence in cryptographic implementations.

timeline.event: Co-authors a public-key cryptosystem paper with Jacques Stern.
Co-authors work on monotone signatures for practical deployment contexts.
Participates in CASCADE research on cryptography for embedded-system security.
